rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī rebukes those who reject judgment by an oath and one witness despite sound reports and early authorities' practice.
rows.anchor: مع شهرة الأحاديث وصحتها بدعوا من عمل بها حتى نقضوا حكمه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The Prophet ruled by an oath together with one witness; ʿAmr ibn Dīnār restricts the report to property cases.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه قضى باليمين مع الشاهد.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr calls the report's chain the soundest and its transmitters trustworthy, citing Muslim and other critics.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: هذا أصح إسناد لهذا الحديث، وهو حديث لا مطعن

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: One report from al-Zuhrī calls judgment by oath and witness an innovation and insists on two witnesses; another says he first ruled by it.
rows.anchor: سألت الزهري عن اليمين مع الشاهد فقال هذا شيء أحدثه الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī endorses the majority position allowing an oath with one witness, based on transmitted reports and generations of Medinan practice; Mālik allowed it in every region.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي لا يجوز عندي خلافه، لتواتر الآثار به عن النبي

rows.speaker: يحيى بن يحيى
rows.claim: In al-Andalus, Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said he had not seen al-Layth issue a ruling or hold the doctrine, thereby opposing Mālik and Medinan practice.
rows.anchor: فإن يحيى بن يحيى زعم أنه لم ير الليث يفتي به ولا يذهب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophetic Sunnah may add rulings to the Qurʾān, as in prohibited marriage combinations, foods, and wiping over footwear alongside Qurʾānic wording.
rows.anchor: لأن السنة مبينة للكتاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān's general permission for sales cannot abrogate the Prophet's bans on uncertain and nonexistent sales; Sunnah explains scripture.
rows.anchor: عن المزابنة وبيع الغرر وبيع مالم يخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although one might call the oath-and-witness ruling case-specific, al-Qurṭubī reads it as establishing a general legal rule.
rows.anchor: بل ذلك عبارة عن تقعيد هذه القاعدة

rows.speaker: أبو داود
rows.claim: A report of Ibn ʿAbbās transmitted by Abū Dāwūd expressly says the Prophet judged by one witness and an oath in rights cases.
rows.anchor: ما رواه أبو داود في حديث ابن عباس أن رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By analogy, an oath has stronger evidentiary standing than two women because women have no role in mutual imprecation, whereas an oath does.
rows.anchor: أنا وجدنا اليمين أقوى من المرأتين، لأنهما لا مدخل لهما في اللعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once sound Sunnah is established, it must be followed and needs no supporting precedent; those who oppose it are answered by it.
rows.anchor: وإذا صحت السنة فالقول بها يجب

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد عبد الوهاب
rows.claim: Among jurists accepting oath-plus-witness, its use is limited by consensus to property and related rights, not bodily rights; property rights are lower because women's testimony is accepted there.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الوهاب: ذلك في الأموال وما يتعلق بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mālik has two reports about intentional injury: one allows a choice between retaliation and compensation, while the sounder report allows neither because bodily rights are involved.
rows.anchor: لا يجب به شيء لأنه من حقوق الأبدان. قال: وهو الصحيح.

rows.speaker: المازري
rows.claim: Al-Māzarī reports agreement on oath-plus-witness for pure money claims and rejection for marriage or divorce as such; claims leading only to money are disputed.
rows.anchor: وقال المازري: يقبل في المال المحض من غير خلاف، ولا يقبل في النكاح

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawī says most jurists reject women's testimony in criminal penalties, marriage, and divorce, and do not let them transmit testimony where they cannot testify directly.
rows.anchor: وقال المهدوي: شهادة النساء في الحدود غير جائزة في قول عامة الفقهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mālik's school accepts two women's testimony in matters unavailable to other witnesses, such as childbirth and a newborn's first cry, though details are disputed.
rows.anchor: ويقضى بأثنتين منهن في كل ما لا يحضره غيرهن كالولادة والاستهلال

rows.speaker: ابن بكير
rows.claim: Ibn Bukayr and others take the address requiring approved witnesses to be directed to judges.
rows.anchor: قال ابن بكير وغيره: هذه مخاطبة للحكام.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects limiting the address to judges: it addresses everyone, although judges carry out the case in practice.
rows.anchor: ابن عطية: وهذا غير نبيل، وإنما الخطاب لجميع الناس

rows.speaker: جمهور
rows.claim: The majority infer that probity is an additional qualification beyond being Muslim, since the verse requires witnesses whom people approve.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الجمهور

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa regards any apparently Muslim person free of manifest wrongdoing as upright, even when character is unknown.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: كل مسلم ظاهر الإسلام مع السلامة من فسق ظاهر

rows.speaker: شريح وعثمان البتى وأبو ثور
rows.claim: Shurayḥ, ʿUthmān al-Battī, and Abū Thawr count Muslims as upright witnesses even if enslaved.
rows.anchor: وقال شريح وعثمان البتى وأبو ثور: هم عدول المسلمين وإن كانوا عبيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Bedouin may testify for a town-dweller if upright: Qurʾānic general wording does not distinguish them, and al-Qurṭubī rejects a restrictive report.
rows.anchor: والصحيح جواز شهادته إذا كان عدلا مرضيا

rows.speaker: مالك وأحمد بن حنبل
rows.claim: Mālik in one report and Aḥmad reject a Bedouin's testimony for a town-dweller, relying on a report from Abū Hurayra.
rows.anchor: وذهب أحمد بن حنبل ومالك في رواية ابن وهب عنه إلى رد شهادة البدوي

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: Probity means religious steadiness: avoiding major sins, preserving respectable conduct and avoiding minor sins, while appearing trustworthy and alert; another definition stresses apparent integrity.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: العدالة هي الاعتدال في الأحوال الدينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because testimony is a grave authority that makes another person liable, God requires approved and upright witnesses with distinguishing qualities.
rows.anchor: شرط تعالى فيها الرضا والعدالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requirement of witness approval supports inference from signs and entrusts judges with discretion to detect carelessness or suspicion and reject testimony.
rows.anchor: دليل على جواز الاجتهاد والاستدلال بالأمارات والعلامات

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa accepts apparent Muslim status as enough in property cases but not criminal penalties.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: يكتفى بظاهر الإسلام في الأموال دون الحدود

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī calls that distinction self-defeating: a property claim is a right and should not receive weaker witness scrutiny than a criminal penalty.
rows.anchor: فلا يكتفى في الشهادة عليه بظاهر الدين كالحدود قاله ابن العربي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Upright witnesses are even more important for marriage than debt, given its effects on lawful status, punishment, and lineage; al-Qurṭubī rejects Abū Ḥanīfa's view.
rows.anchor: فاشتراطها في النكاح أولى، خلافا لأبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apparent profession of Islam does not establish probity, since impressive speech or appearance may conceal disqualifying conduct.
rows.anchor: ولا يغتر بظاهر قوله: أنا مسلم

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayd glosses the verb for straying as forgetting; in testimony, a witness may recall one part while forgetting another and become uncertain.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: معنى تضل تنسى

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads the particle with kasra as a conditional; the following clause answers it and the phrase describes the witnesses.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «إن» بكسر الهمزة على معنى الجزاء

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Under Ḥamza's conditional reading, Sībawayh parses the following verb as a new clause; with the open particle it is an object of purpose with an omitted governor.
rows.anchor: هذا قول سيبويه. ومن فتح «أن» فهي مفعول له

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās allows several vocalizations of the verb, including forms reflecting the dialect that says ḍalaltu taḍillu.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس ويجوز «تضل» بفتح التاء والضاد، ويجوز تضل

rows.speaker: الجحدري وعيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read the verb with a pattern meaning that one forgets.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وعيسى بن عمر «أن تضل» بضم التاء وفتح الضاد

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqāsh reports another al-Jaḥdarī reading, with the testimony itself going astray or being lost.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش عن الجحدري ضم التاء وكسر الضاد بمعنى أن تضل الشهادة

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna and Abū ʿAmr understand the lighter reading of the reminder verb as returning a woman's testimony to memory, so two women's testimony totals a man's.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī finds the lighter reminder reading less apt: a reminder naturally answers forgetfulness, and the doubled reading means one woman alerts the other when she forgets.
rows.anchor: قلت: وإليها ترجع قراءة أبي عمرو، أي إن تنس إحداهما

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the command not to refuse witnesses covers both being asked to record testimony and to deliver testimony already held.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: جمعت هذه الآية أمرين، وهما ألا تأبى إذا دعيت

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع وابن عباس
rows.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and Ibn ʿAbbās interpret the summons as a request to bear witness and enter it in writing.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة والربيع وابن عباس: أي لتحملها وإثباتها في الكتاب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid interprets the summons as a request to give testimony already held; he and others say an initial invitation to witness may be declined.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معنى الآية إذا دعيت إلى أداء شهادة وقد حصلت عندك

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats assistance as recommended when witnesses are plentiful, increasingly urgent when rights may be lost, and obligatory when delay will destroy a right.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والآية كما قال الحسن جمعت أمرين على جهة الندب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī infers that a ruler may employ public witnesses and support them from the treasury to preserve people's rights; this is public support like judges' salaries, not a fee.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن جائزا للإمام أن يقيم للناس شهودا ويجعل لهم من بيت المال كفايتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indicates that witnesses go to the judge when summoned, a practice established across legal traditions and reflected in a proverb.
rows.anchor: دل على أن الشاهد هو الذي يمشي إلى الحاكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An enslaved person is excluded from the witness class because he cannot independently answer a summons, just as he lacks independent authority in other duties.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا يمكنه أن يجيب، ولا يصح له أن يأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī rejects the view that testimony already held is merely recommended: it is obligatory when a right risks loss, supported by Qurʾānic commands and the Prophet's call to aid the wronged.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن أداءها فرض وإن لم يسألها إذا خاف على الحق ضياعه

rows.speaker: ابن القاسم
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qāsim and others say refusing a required testimony damages the witness and testimony generally, whether the right belongs to God or a person.
rows.anchor: هذا قول ابن القاسم وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī prefers general disqualification: wrongful refusal is misconduct that removes eligibility for testimony altogether.
rows.anchor: والصحيح الأول لأن الذي يوجب جرحته إنما هو فسقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise of witnesses who volunteer testimony does not conflict with a report condemning people who testify without being asked; the latter has three possible readings.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث محمول على ثلاثة أوجه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Shayba reports that ʿUmar warned of later false testimony, distinguishing corrupt witnesses from truthful help preserving rights.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه خطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation is that greed or bias makes a person eagerly present testimony before being asked; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī reports that boys were warned against contracts and testimony.
rows.anchor: يحمله الشره على تنفيذ ما يشهد به

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the verb for becoming weary as boredom and gives its verbal nouns; an unnamed poet illustrates weariness after eighty years of life.
rows.anchor: معناه تملوا. قال الأخفش: يقال سئمت أسأم سأما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The writing phrase is accusative after the verb, and small or large are circumstantial descriptions; small comes first for emphasis, since people might neglect tiny debts.
rows.anchor: وقدم الصغير اهتماما به

rows.speaker: علماؤنا
rows.claim: The jurists except a tiny amount such as a qirat because people do not normally care to affirm or deny it.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا: إلا ما كان من قيراط ونحوه لنزارته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's terms mean fairest, soundest and most protective for testimony, closer, and that people should not doubt.
rows.anchor: معناه أعدل، يعني أن يكتب القليل والكثير ويشهد عليه

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says most scholars reject testimony based solely on handwriting when the witness no longer remembers; Mālik argues from Joseph's report.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: أكثر من يحفظ عنه من أهل العلم يمنع أن يشهد الشاهد

rows.speaker: ابن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak approves the report that a witness may testify from a document bearing his mark or handwriting even if he forgot the testimony.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المبارك: استحسنت هذا جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports of the Prophet's judgments and earlier prophets support accepting reliable signs and indications as evidence.
rows.anchor: حكم في أشياء غير واحدة بالدلائل والشواهد

rows.speaker: الأخفش أبو سعيد
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the exception as a sale that occurs immediately; other grammarians parse its predicate differently, while ʿĀṣim reads an implicit subject.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش أبو سعيد: أي إلا أن تقع تجارة، فكان بمعنى وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God lifts writing requirements for cash exchanges, commonly small purchases, because writing them would be burdensome; al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk specify hand-to-hand sales.
rows.anchor: نص على ترك ذلك ورفع الجناح فيه في كل مبايعة بنقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Immediate reciprocal possession reduces disputes, while real estate and animals are less readily transferred or hidden; deferred transactions need written safeguards against changed circumstances and distrust.
rows.anchor: فكان الكتاب توثقا لما عسى أن يطرأ من اختلاف الأحوال وتغير القلوب

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī classifies sales as documented with witnesses, secured by a pledge, or based on trust, reading the verse as evidence for these forms.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي: البيوع ثلاثة: بيع بكتاب وشهود، وبيع برهان

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar would obtain witnesses for cash sales and write down deferred sales.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عمر إذا باع بنقد أشهد، وإذا باع بنسيئة كتب

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reads the witnessing command as covering small and large sales; Abū Mūsā, Ibn ʿUmar, and others hold it obligatory, and ʿAṭāʾ demands witnesses for tiny purchases.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: معناه وأشهدوا على صغير ذلك وكبيره

rows.speaker: الشعبي والحسن
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and al-Ḥasan treat witnessing as recommendation and guidance rather than a binding duty; Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and other jurists are also said to hold this.
rows.anchor: وذهب الشعبي والحسن إلى أن ذلك على الندب والإرشاد لا على الحتم

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says the recommendation is the view of all jurists and is correct.
rows.anchor: وزعم ابن العربي أن هذا قول الكافة، قال: وهو الصحيح

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says only al-Ḍaḥḥāk is reported to require witnessing; the Prophet made and recorded sales without witnesses and pledged his armor without them.
rows.anchor: ولم يحك عن أحد ممن قال بالوجوب إلا الضحاك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī notes that the obligation was attributed to several authorities besides al-Ḍaḥḥāk, correcting Ibn al-ʿArabī's account.
rows.anchor: قلت: قد ذكرنا الوجوب عن غير الضحاك.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds mandatory witnessing impractical for small sales and sometimes socially awkward; he treats it as recommended for its usual benefit unless an excuse intervenes.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو محمد بن عطية: والوجوب في ذلك قلق، أما في الدقائق فصعب شاق

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥakam, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd are reported to say that the mutual-trust clause abrogated witnessing sales.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذا قول الحسن والحكم وعبد الرحمن بن زيد

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects abrogation: the pledge clause addresses inability to find a scribe and an unrequired pledge, a different case from writing and witnessing.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: وهذا لا معنى له لأن هذا حكم غير الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Later rules for different situations do not abrogate earlier rules; some note both clauses may have been revealed together, since abrogation cannot occur simultaneously.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يرد الناسخ والمنسوخ معا جميعا في حالة واحدة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the debt verse is established, not abrogated, and writing, pledges, and witnesses are alternative means of securing debt; witnessing is recommended like pledging.
rows.anchor: قال: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال لما قيل له: إن آية الدين منسوخة قال: لا والله إن آية الدين محكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says explicit Sunnah showing the Prophet accepted a sale without witnesses is an even stronger argument against mandatory witnessing.
rows.anchor: وأحسن منه ما جاء من صريح السنة في ترك الإشهاد

rows.speaker: طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي
rows.claim: Ṭāriq ibn ʿAbd Allāh recounts selling a camel to a man later identified as the Prophet; the Prophet sent word for the sellers to take dates and eat until satisfied, without witnesses at the sale.
rows.anchor: وهو ما خرجه الدارقطني عن طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي قال

rows.speaker: عمارة بن خزيمة
rows.claim: ʿUmāra ibn Khuzayma reports that his Companion uncle witnessed the Prophet's purchase of a horse from a Bedouin, and Khuzayma ibn Thābit testified from trust in the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن عمارة بن خزيمة أن عمه حدثه وهو من أصحاب النبي

rows.speaker: خزيمة بن ثابت
rows.claim: The Prophet made Khuzayma's testimony count as that of two men because he testified on the basis of believing the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال خزيمة بن ثابت: أنا أشهد أنك قد بعته. فأقبل النبي

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وطاوس وابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Ṭāwūs, and Ibn Zayd say a scribe must write only what is dictated and a witness must neither add to nor subtract from testimony.
rows.anchor: لا يكتب الكاتب ما لم يمل عليه، ولا يزيد الشاهد في شهادته ولا ينقص منها. قاله الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ interpret the prohibition as forbidding a scribe or witness from refusing when asked to serve.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء أن المعنى لا يمتنع الكاتب أن يكتب

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās reports Abū Isḥāq's preference for the reading that forbids falsifying a record or testimony, since the warning of sin fits dishonesty better than burdening a busy witness.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: ورأيت أبا إسحاق يميل إلى هذا القول

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وطاوس والسدي
rows.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ṭāwūs, and al-Suddī understand the verse to forbid harassing a busy scribe or witness who gives a reasonable excuse; Ibn Masʿūd has a similar reading.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك وطاوس والسدي وروي عن ابن عباس: معنى الآية { ولا يضآر كاتب ولا شهيد }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form encompasses both kinds of harm: dishonest additions and omissions wrongfully affect people and property, while imposing on busy witnesses violates God's command.
rows.anchor: ولفظ المضارة إذ هو من اثنين، يقتضي هذه المعاني

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī explains 'it is wrongdoing by you' as meaning a sinful act; falsifying testimony and imposing on busy witnesses are both disobedience.
rows.anchor: أي معصية عن سفيان الثوري. فالكاتب والشاهد يعصيان بالزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises that reverent people receive understanding and discernment to distinguish truth from falsehood, sometimes placed directly in the heart.
rows.anchor: يجعل في قلبه نورا يفهم به ما يلقى إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that piety gives believers discernment is linked to the verse promising a criterion by which to distinguish right from wrong.
rows.anchor: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When writing is prevented by an excuse, a pledge protects property; travel is common, but any impediment qualifies, including a busy time or nighttime, and concern about the debtor may justify security.
rows.anchor: وجعل لها الرهن، ونص من أحوال العذر على السفر الذي هو غالب الأعذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet pledged his armor with a Jewish seller for barley; he insisted that he was trustworthy and would repay, yet died while the armor remained pledged.
rows.anchor: فمات ودرعه مرهونة صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: جمهور من العلماء
rows.claim: The majority permit pledges during travel by Qurʾānic text and in settled places by the Prophet's practice; al-Qurṭubī also reads the verse by analogy to any excuse.
rows.anchor: قال جمهور من العلماء: الرهن في السفر بنص التنزيل، وفي الحضر ثابت بسنة الرسول

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وداود
rows.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Dāwūd restrict pledges to travel, but al-Qurṭubī rejects their inference because the verse describes the usual case rather than prohibiting pledges elsewhere.
rows.anchor: سوى مجاهد والضحاك وداود، متمسكين بالآية

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet bought food on credit from a Jew and pledged his iron armor; Ibn ʿAbbās reports it remained pledged at his death for thirty measures of barley.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اشترى من يهودي طعاما إلى أجل

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers have the singular 'writer'; Ibn ʿAbbās and others read a plural understood as writing materials, scribes, or lack of tools, with grammarians offering different analyses.
rows.anchor: قرأ الجمهور «كاتبا» بمعنى رجل يكتب

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls the alternative reading rare; Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds it apt for varied cases, and al-Qurṭubī says both readings work apart from the codex spelling.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: هذه القراءة شاذة والعامة على خلافها

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وابن كثير
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn Kathīr read rahun; other readings include ruhun and ruhan, with grammarians disputing whether these are plural forms or collective nouns.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن كثير «فرهن» بضم الراء والهاء

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawī parses 'pledges' as a subject with an omitted predicate: possessed pledges suffice for security.
rows.anchor: وقال المهدوي: «فرهان» ابتداء والخبر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pledge is property retained as security so a creditor can recover from its price or proceeds if collection from the debtor fails; the Arabic root also means permanence and continuity.
rows.anchor: معنى الرهن: احتباس العين وثيقة بالحق ليستوفى الحق من ثمنها

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī says the small plural of rahn is unattested; if it existed, its pattern would be afʿāl, as in kalb and aklab.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: وتكسير «رهن» على أقل العدد لم أعلمه جاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي وأبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī and Abū Zayd distinguish forms of the pledge verb: arhantu is used for bidding high, while raḥantu is used for loans and sales.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي: أرهنت في المغالاة، وأما في القرض والبيع فرهنت

rows.speaker: الزجاج وابن الأعرابي والأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj, Ibn al-Aʿrābī, and al-Akhfash also allow both raḥantu and arhantu for pledging.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يقال في الرهن: رهنت وأرهنت وقاله ابن الأعرابي والأخفش

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن همام السلولي
rows.claim: A verse by ʿAbd Allāh ibn Hammām al-Salūlī uses arhantu; most transmitters retain that form, while al-Aṣmaʿī reads a present-tense verb after the past and explains the wāw as circumstantial.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله بن همام السلولي: فلما خشيت أظافيرهم نجوت وأرهنتهم مالكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledged person is the one receiving the pledge; an object may be called marhūn or rahīn, a woman rahīna, and rahantu is standard for pledging in a sale or loan.
rows.anchor: ويقال بلا خلاف في البيع والقرض: رهنت رهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qurṭubī adopts the view that a pledge ends if it voluntarily returns to the pledgor, following the requirement that it be possessed; Abū Ḥanīfa exempts return as a loan or deposit, while al-Shāfiʿī preserves the earlier possession.
rows.anchor: قلت هذا هو المعتمد عندنا في أن الرهن متى رجع إلى الراهن باختيار المرتهن بطل الرهن

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says a pledge made verbally but never physically possessed creates no legal effect, because the verse predicates the ruling on possession.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي: لم يجعل الله الحكم إلا برهن موصوف بالقبض

rows.speaker: المالكية
rows.claim: The Mālikīs say the contract binds the pledgor and require delivery; possession completes the pledge's benefit, while two other schools make it a condition of bindingness and validity.
rows.anchor: وقالت المالكية: يلزم الرهن بالعقد ويجبر الراهن على دفع الرهن

rows.speaker: المالكية
rows.claim: The Mālikīs support the pledge's binding contract by commands to fulfill contracts and promises, and the Prophetic rule that believers fulfill their conditions.
rows.anchor: وهذا شرط، فالقبض عندنا شرط في كمال فائدته

rows.speaker: جمهور العلماء
rows.claim: Possession by a neutral custodian counts as receipt because the custodian represents the creditor; Ibn Abī Laylā, Qatāda, al-Ḥakam, and ʿAṭāʾ require the creditor to hold it.
rows.anchor: وقول الجمهور أصح من جهة المعنى لأنه إذا صار عند العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If collateral with a neutral custodian is lost, neither creditor nor custodian is liable: the creditor never possessed it and the custodian is a trustee.
rows.anchor: والأمين غير ضامن. العاشرة لما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir argues that a Ḥanafī exception allowing two creditors jointly to take a plot as collateral concedes that a share in common property may be pledged.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: وهذا إجازة رهن المشاع لأن كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: ابن المنذر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir considers pledging jointly owned property valid just as selling it is valid; al-Qurṭubī's school permits it against Abū Ḥanīfa's school.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: رهن المشاع جائز كما يجوز بيعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mālikīs permit pledging a debt owed by another: anything saleable may be collateral, and a debt has value, though opponents say it cannot be physically possessed or directly realized.
rows.anchor: الحادية عشرة ورهن ما في الذمة جائز عند علمائنا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Al-Bukhārī transmits from Abū Hurayra the Prophet's rule that an animal pledged as collateral may be ridden and its milk drunk in return for the expense borne by the user.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī says the first wording does not identify whether the pledgor, creditor, or custodian may ride and milk the pledged animal.
rows.anchor: قال الخطابي: هذا كلام مبهم ليس في نفس اللفظ بيان

rows.speaker: أحمد وإسحاق
rows.claim: A more explicit Abū Hurayra report says the creditor who feeds a pledged animal may ride or drink its milk in proportion to the expense; Aḥmad and Isḥāq adopt that rule.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أحمد وإسحاق: أن المرتهن ينتفع من الرهن بالحلب والركوب

rows.speaker: أبو ثور
rows.claim: Abū Thawr permits a creditor who maintained neglected collateral to ride it or use an enslaved servant; al-Awzāʿī and al-Layth share this view.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو ثور: إذا كان الراهن ينفق عليه لم ينتفع به المرتهن

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report says a pledge cannot be foreclosed and its owner receives its yield and bears its loss; Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, al-Shaʿbī, and Ibn Sīrīn hold that benefits belong to its owner, who pays upkeep.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khaṭṭābī considers the view that collateral's benefits belong to its owner strongest, supported by the explicit wording about its yield and loss.
rows.anchor: قال الخطابي: وهو أولى الأقوال وأصحها

rows.speaker: الطحاوي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭaḥāwī argues the permissive benefit report came before the prohibition of usury; al-Shaʿbī argues it was abrogated, since even a pledged enslaved woman may not be used.
rows.anchor: وقال الطحاوي: كان ذلك وقت كون الربا مباحا

rows.speaker: ابن عبد البر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr says scholars agree the pledged animal's milk and use belong to its owner; use without permission is barred, while permission raises issues of unknown benefit and usury.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عبد البر وقد أجمعوا أن لبن الرهن وظهره للراهن

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuwayzimandād says a creditor may stipulate use of collateral in a sale or lease, but not a loan, where it would be a loan yielding benefit and thus usury.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن خويز منداد: ولو شرط المرتهن الانتفاع بالرهن فلذلك حالتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pledge may not be stipulated to become the creditor's property if the debtor misses the due date; this pre-Islamic foreclosure practice was abolished by the Prophetic report.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز غلق الرهن، وهو أن يشترط المرتهن أنه له بحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report is read with an indicative nominative ending: the pledge does not become foreclosed; the Arabic expression also describes a closed door or unredeemed collateral.
rows.anchor: هكذا قيدناه برفع القاف على الخبر، أي ليس يغلق الرهن

rows.speaker: أبو عمر
rows.claim: Abū ʿUmar says a connected chain for the report may be mistaken: Ismāʿīl did not hear from Ibn Abī Dhiʾb directly, but via weak ʿAbbād; the report's basis is mursal.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر: لم يسمعه إسماعيل من ابن أبي ذئب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's basis among hadith critics is mursal, although it has many connected routes they criticize; the wording about yield and loss is also disputed.
rows.anchor: وأصل هذا الحديث عند أهل العلم بالنقل مرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Collateral growth inseparable from the property, such as fattening or offspring, follows the pledge; crops, milk, wool, and fruit do not unless stipulated because they are independently treated for alms.
rows.anchor: وما عدا ذلك من غلة وثمرة ولبن وصوف فلا يدخل فيه إلا أن يشترطه

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Mālik and many jurists give a secured creditor priority over other creditors when a debtor not declared insolvent pledges an asset; al-Qurṭubī rejects another report giving all creditors a share.
rows.anchor: ويكون المرتهن أحق بالرهن من الغرماء قاله مالك وجماعة من الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the debtor is trusted, the creditor must allow payment without delay; the imperative is obligatory by consensus, enforceable judgments, and sound reports.
rows.anchor: وهو أمر معناه الوجوب، بقرينة الإجماع على وجوب أداء الديون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: 'His trust' refers to the debt owed by the debtor, named as a verbal noun and attributed to him, as in the verse about not giving property to the foolish.
rows.anchor: الأمانة مصدر سمى به الشيء الذي في الذمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a witness must testify wherever summoned and disclose testimony wherever questioned, rather than reserve it only for a ruler.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: على الشاهد أن يشهد حيثما استشهد، ويخبر حيثما استخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on concealing testimony is obligatory when a right may be lost; testimony is a collective duty, and a claimant's request makes it incumbent on needed witnesses.
rows.anchor: نهى الشاهد عن أن يضر بكتمان الشهادة، وهو نهي على الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is singled out because concealment begins there; naming the part for the whole intensifies the warning, and the clause admits several grammatical parses.
rows.anchor: خص القلب بالذكر إذ الكتم من أفعاله

rows.speaker: الكيا
rows.claim: Al-Kiyā says intending to withhold testimony and then not speaking makes sin apply to resolve and speech; calling the heart sinful is forceful rhetoric.
rows.anchor: وقال الكيا: لما عزم على ألا يؤديها وترك أداءها باللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing and testimony protect social relations from disputes, denial, and demanding more than is owed; uncertain sales, gambling, and wine are barred because they breed hostility.
rows.anchor: لمراعاة صلاح ذات البين ونفى التنازع المؤدي إلى فساد ذات البين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following God's commands and prohibitions brings well-being in this world and religion.
rows.anchor: فمن تأدب بأدب الله في أوامره وزواجره حاز صلاح الدنيا والدين

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet says God repays for one who takes people's money intending repayment and destroys the one who takes it intending to squander it.
rows.anchor: روى البخاري عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ميمونة
rows.claim: Maymūna reports that God helps a person who borrows intending repayment; another report warns debt can frighten people after they felt secure.
rows.anchor: وروى النسائي: عن ميمونة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنها استدانت، فقيل: يا أم المؤمنين

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet's prayer seeking refuge from anxiety, incapacity, miserliness, the burden of debt, and domination by others; scholars explain the burden as inability to repay.
rows.anchor: وروى البخاري عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دعاء ذكره
